en.seoTitle: Codex Open Source: Context, Tool Loops, and Agent Workflows
en.description: Study Codex’s open agent harness to improve your own workflows: connect tools to task context, carry state across steps, and define review boundaries. Use its runtime and integration design as a reference for work in Floatboat.
overview: Codex is OpenAI’s coding agent and open agent harness. The public project provides the surrounding execution system: it helps an agent inspect a workspace, maintain a conversation, use tools, and carry a task through successive steps. The harness is the software around a model, rather than the model weights.

For a Floatboat user, the useful question is which part of a workflow needs a stronger execution loop. Codex offers a concrete reference for connecting task context, tools, feedback, and human approval. Reusing its software is one option; applying these design principles to an existing workflow is another.

The repository uses Apache-2.0. OpenAI’s models, subscriptions, and managed services have their own access and commercial terms. Publishing the harness makes its implementation inspectable; it does not promise that every hosted Codex feature is included in a local checkout.
en.capabilitiesTitle: Workflow Mechanisms to Learn From
en.capabilitiesIntro: Codex separates continuing task context, controlled tool use, and runtime integration surfaces. Compare those mechanisms as references for your own workflow, distinguishing how work is executed from the interface through which a person or application requests it.

capabilities.title: Context that follows the task
capabilities.description: Use its context and conversation model as a reference for preserving inputs, decisions, and tool feedback across a multi-step workflow.

capabilities.title: A controlled tool loop
capabilities.description: Study how tool results influence the next action, then define where your workflow should continue automatically and where a person must review.

capabilities.title: Runtime integration choices
capabilities.description: Compare CLI, SDK, and app-server responsibilities when deciding whether an existing workflow needs a bounded task or an ongoing agent session.

useCases.title: Use Cases for Codex
useCases.description: Research delivery, repeatable coding, and application integration expose different execution boundaries. Use Codex as a reference for connecting context, tool results, and acceptance points, then assess which CLI, SDK, or app-server interface fits your workflow.

items.title: A research-to-deliverable workflow
items.description: A research workflow can borrow Codex's context–tool–review pattern to connect source reading with a checked draft. Define the delivery format, retain the evidence behind conclusions, and identify decisions requiring human confirmation. The execution design should show how the draft reaches its final acceptance step.

items.title: A repeatable coding task
items.description: For recurring repository work, specify the task, permitted files, and test commands before separating investigation, implementation, verification, and approval. Each stage should leave an inspectable result. The reusable brief then gives the next coding task the same clear boundaries without assuming its code changes will be identical.

items.title: An agent in your own workspace
items.description: An application that owns its business context and permitted operations needs an integration surface that fits that responsibility. Compare the documented CLI, SDK, and app-server interfaces against the task entry points and context sources. Choose a candidate and define a minimal compatibility test before committing to the integration.

items.title: Bound investigation before modification
items.description: A repository task may need broad reading but only a narrow set of permitted edits. Use Codex's controlled tool-loop design as a reference for separating those stages, with explicit evidence required before moving from investigation to action. Describe the review point in your own workflow and test the boundary rather than assuming a model choice alone restricts what the runtime can do.

faq.question: Is Codex a model or an agent harness?
faq.answer: The open-source Codex project is an agent and harness implementation. It organizes context, tools, and task execution around model calls. The models it can access are a separate part of the system.

faq.question: How do the CLI, SDK, and app-server differ?
faq.answer: The CLI is a direct interactive interface. The SDK supports programmatic agent workflows, while app-server exposes a session protocol for applications that need ongoing conversations, events, and approval handling.

faq.question: Does the source include free model access?
faq.answer: No. Apache-2.0 covers the project source. Model access, subscription entitlements, API usage, and managed services follow their own terms and can have separate charges or limits.

faq.question: Can Codex be built into a different interface?
faq.answer: OpenAI documents app-server and SDK integration for that purpose. The application supplies its own interface and relevant context, and should define what tools the agent can use and which actions need review.

faq.question: Does an open harness include every hosted feature?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. The public runtime and integration surfaces are distinct from hosted infrastructure, account features, and model services. Verify the particular feature in its official documentation.

faq.question: Must I switch products to use these workflow ideas?
faq.answer: No. You can first use Codex as a reference for task structure, tool boundaries, and result review in your existing workflow. Reusing software is a separate choice that requires compatibility, permissions, and license checks; applying the design ideas does not automatically connect the software to Floatboat.

howTo.title: Validate a Codex-style execution loop
howTo.description: Adapting an execution loop starts with one bottleneck in your existing task. Define its inputs, tools, and approval points, then test a small complete cycle before deciding which Codex interfaces or runtime ideas are worth adopting more broadly.

items.title: Map one workflow bottleneck
items.description: Identify the missing context, tool, state transition, or approval point before choosing a runtime component.

items.title: Define the contract and boundaries
items.description: Write down the task input, permitted tools, expected output, and human decisions for that step.

items.title: Validate a small complete loop
items.description: Test representative inputs and review the resulting evidence, changes, and failure behavior before expanding the workflow.

en.seoDescription: Study Codex’s context handling, tool loop, and approval model. Compare CLI, SDK, and app-server roles when designing or extending your own agent workflows.

zh.seoTitle: Codex 开源项目：上下文、工具循环与 Agent 工作流
zh.description: 参考 Codex 的开放 Agent Harness，为自己的工作流设计工具连接、任务状态与审阅边界。围绕 Floatboat 中的资料处理、任务执行和结果交付，判断哪些运行机制与集成方式值得复用。
overview: Codex 是 OpenAI 的编程 Agent 与开放 Agent Harness。公开项目提供模型周围的执行系统，让 Agent 理解工作区、维持对话、调用工具并逐步推进任务。这里的 harness 指运行与协作软件，不等同于模型权重。
对 Floatboat 用户而言，重点是判断自己的工作流在哪个环节需要更清晰的执行循环。Codex 为连接任务上下文、工具、反馈与人工审批提供了具体参考；可以评估软件组件的复用，也可以先将这些设计原则用于现有流程。
仓库采用 Apache-2.0 许可。OpenAI 模型、订阅和托管服务有独立的访问与商业条款。开放 harness 让实现可被查看和扩展，但不能据此承诺本地源码包含所有托管 Codex 功能。
zh.capabilitiesTitle: 值得借鉴的工作流机制
zh.capabilitiesIntro: 持续上下文、受控工具循环和运行层接口共同组成 Codex 的执行参考。人或应用发起任务的入口，与任务内部怎样推进属于不同职责，借鉴机制时需要结合自己的工作流分别评估。

capabilities.title: 随任务延续的上下文
capabilities.description: 参考其上下文与会话组织方式，为多步骤工作流保留输入、决策和工具反馈，减少每一步重新解释任务的成本。

capabilities.title: 有边界的工具循环
capabilities.description: 研究工具结果如何影响下一步，再明确自己的流程哪些步骤可以继续执行、哪些节点需要人工审阅。

capabilities.title: 运行层集成选择
capabilities.description: 比较 CLI、SDK 与 app-server 的职责，判断现有工作流需要一次性任务，还是能够持续推进的 Agent 会话。

useCases.title: Codex的使用场景
useCases.description: 研究资料变成草稿、仓库任务变成修改，以及 Agent 接入自有应用，都需要不同执行边界。Codex 的上下文和工具机制可供参考，审阅证据及接口选择则应结合自己的任务定义。

items.title: 从研究资料到交付成果
items.description: 研究工作流可以借鉴 Codex 连接上下文、工具与审阅的方式，将来源阅读衔接到经过核对的草稿。明确交付格式，保留结论背后的证据，并标出需要人工确认的决定。执行设计应说明草稿如何形成，以及最后由谁完成验收。

items.title: 可重复的代码任务
items.description: 对于反复出现的仓库工作，先写明任务、允许修改的文件和测试命令，再划分调查、实施、验证与批准环节。每一阶段都留下可以检查的结果，形成可复用的代码任务说明。复用的是清楚的边界，而不是要求不同任务产生相同修改。

items.title: 自己的工作空间中的 Agent
items.description: 如果自有应用需要掌握业务上下文和允许执行的操作，应根据这些职责选择集成方式。对照任务入口、可用操作与资料来源，比较官方文档中的 CLI、SDK 和 app-server 接口，再通过最小兼容性测试验证候选方案，而不是直接假定它适合现有环境。

items.title: 区分只读调查与允许修改
items.description: 仓库任务可能需要较广阅读，却只允许修改很小范围。可以参考 Codex 的受控工具循环划分阶段，明确从调查进入行动前需要什么证据。在自己的工作流中设计审阅节点并验证边界，不假定仅仅选择某个模型就能限制运行时可执行的操作。

faq.question: Codex 是模型还是 Agent Harness？
faq.answer: Codex 的开源项目提供 Agent 与 harness 实现，负责组织上下文、工具和任务执行。它使用的模型属于系统的另一部分，不能把运行层开源理解为模型权重也在此仓库中。

faq.question: CLI、SDK 和 app-server 有什么区别？
faq.answer: CLI 面向直接交互，SDK 用于程序化 Agent 工作流，app-server 则为需要持续对话、事件流和审批处理的应用提供会话协议。选择取决于使用场景，不必同时使用全部入口。

faq.question: 源码许可是否包含免费模型调用？
faq.answer: 不包含。Apache-2.0 适用于项目源码；模型访问、订阅权益、API 调用和托管服务各自有独立条款，可能存在费用和使用限制。

faq.question: Codex 能嵌入自己的应用界面吗？
faq.answer: 可以。OpenAI 提供 app-server 与 SDK 集成说明，由应用提供界面和相关上下文，并明确 Agent 可使用哪些工具、哪些操作需要人工审阅。

faq.question: 开放 harness 是否包含全部托管功能？
faq.answer: 不一定。公开运行层与集成入口不同于托管基础设施、账户功能和模型服务，具体功能是否属于源码范围，应查阅对应官方文档。

faq.question: 借鉴这些机制是否需要更换工作工具？
faq.answer: 不需要。可以先将 Codex 作为任务结构、工具边界和结果审阅的设计参考，在已有工作流中验证思路。软件复用是另一项选择，需要核对兼容性、权限与许可；借鉴设计思路不会自动完成软件与 Floatboat 的连接。

howTo.title: 验证 Codex 式执行循环
howTo.description: 一项实际瓶颈比完整复制运行时更适合作为起点。明确输入、工具和批准节点，用小型任务串联执行与审阅，再根据验证结果判断哪些 Codex 接口或机制值得复用。

items.title: 定位一个流程瓶颈
items.description: 先确定缺少的是上下文、工具、状态衔接还是审批节点，再判断是否需要运行层组件。

items.title: 明确输入输出与边界
items.description: 为该环节写明输入、允许使用的工具、预期输出，以及必须由人作出的决定。

items.title: 验证一个小型完整循环
items.description: 使用代表性输入测试完整过程，检查证据、修改与失败行为，再扩大工作流范围。

zh.seoDescription: 研究 Codex 的上下文处理、工具循环与审批机制，比较 CLI、SDK 和 app-server 的职责，为自己的 Agent 工作流选择可参考的执行方式，并核对模型与运行条件。

en.seoTitle: DeepSeek Harness: Plugins, Tool Composition, and Agent Runtimes
en.description: Use DeepSeek Harness as a reference for composing your own agent workflows. Study its plugin architecture to separate model access, tools, and task capabilities, then evaluate focused extensions for work organized in Floatboat.
overview: DeepSeek Harness, also called dsh, is an open-source agent harness developed by DeepSeek. It provides a runtime around model interaction rather than a new model in itself. The project’s central design is to express the system through composable plugins.

Its value for workflow design is the separation of capabilities into composable parts. A Floatboat user can use that idea to identify the tools, context, and responsibilities a task requires before considering a specific plugin or runtime integration. The reference architecture does not establish a ready-made connection to Floatboat.

DeepSeek describes the project as a developer preview with compatibility-breaking changes expected. Its MIT source license is separate from model-provider access and third-party dependencies. Evaluate it as an evolving platform, with version-specific documentation and deliberate workspace boundaries.
en.capabilitiesTitle: Workflow Mechanisms to Learn From
en.capabilitiesIntro: DeepSeek Harness organizes work through distinct capabilities and their composition. Review the boundaries between plugins, the input/output chain of a focused workflow, and the version changes that may affect extensions before applying that structure to recurring work.

capabilities.title: Separate capabilities clearly
capabilities.description: Use the plugin-first architecture to reason about model access, tools, and workflow responsibilities as separate parts.

capabilities.title: Compose a focused workflow
capabilities.description: Evaluate only the capabilities needed by the task, rather than treating a large plugin catalog as a complete working solution.

capabilities.title: Plan for extension changes
capabilities.description: Treat version compatibility as part of workflow design so a runtime update does not silently change the expected behavior.

useCases.title: Use Cases for DeepSeek Harness
useCases.description: Digest pipelines, custom connectors, and small runtime experiments need explicit plugin responsibilities. Compare how DeepSeek Harness separates collection, transformation, and tool access, with compatibility and failure behavior checked before recurring work depends on a composition.

items.title: A modular information workflow
items.description: A news digest can be divided into collection, transformation, and review capabilities. Start with approved public sources, deduplication rules, and the digest's review requirements, then define what each plugin receives and returns. The resulting mapping makes responsibility visible when a source is repeated or a summary needs correction.

items.title: A custom tool connection
items.description: When a workflow lacks a particular external tool, inspect its API documentation alongside the current plugin contract. Define the allowed operations and reference the approved credential source without embedding secrets. A connector design should explain authentication boundaries and failure handling as clearly as the successful tool call.

items.title: A controlled workflow experiment
items.description: A preview-stage runtime should first be assessed with a small composition and representative inputs. Limit the capability set, define acceptable failure behavior, and record what actually happens. Use that experiment to decide whether recurring work has enough evidence for adoption or should remain on hold.

items.title: Assess an extension upgrade
items.description: A changed plugin version can affect more than its own installation step when other capabilities depend on its input and output. Compare the current contract and representative behavior with the proposed version before updating a composition. Record incompatible assumptions and the checks needed for dependent stages, keeping a preview runtime's change risk visible rather than treating the upgrade as a routine replacement.

faq.question: Is DeepSeek Harness an official DeepSeek project?
faq.answer: Yes. It is published in the deepseek-ai organization, and its README explicitly identifies DeepSeek AI as the developer. Use that repository rather than assuming a similarly named community fork is official.

faq.question: What does everything-is-a-plugin mean here?
faq.answer: It describes the project’s Cordis-based composition model. The runtime’s capabilities are assembled through plugins; the actual tools and behavior still depend on the plugins and configuration selected for a session.

faq.question: Is dsh a separate AI model?
faq.answer: No. dsh is the runtime and application entry point. Model inference comes from the provider configured for the session, with that provider’s own credentials, availability, and commercial terms.

faq.question: How stable is the project interface?
faq.answer: The official README marks it as a developer preview and explicitly expects compatibility-breaking changes. Pin and evaluate the version you use instead of assuming an extension will work unchanged across releases.

faq.question: Does MIT cover connected models and services?
faq.answer: MIT applies to the project source. Model APIs, external services, and third-party components retain their own terms, costs, and operational requirements.

faq.question: Must I switch products to use these workflow ideas?
faq.answer: No. You can first use DeepSeek Harness as a reference for task structure, tool boundaries, and result review in your existing workflow. Reusing software is a separate choice that requires compatibility, permissions, and license checks; applying the design ideas does not automatically connect the software to Floatboat.

prerequisites.title: Check DeepSeek Harness extension requirements
prerequisites.description: Different Harness extensions may require different credentials, versions, and runtime dependencies. Check the specific capabilities in the proposed composition rather than preparing a generic plugin environment and assuming that every connection shares the same execution conditions.

items.title: Check a candidate composition
items.description: Review capability boundaries, credentials, and version compatibility for the extensions you actually need.

howTo.title: Design a capability chain with DeepSeek Harness
howTo.description: A plugin composition should follow the task's real processing stages. Map those responsibilities, check extension compatibility, and inspect handoffs and failures in a representative run before expanding the chain or relying on it for repeated delivery.

items.title: List the task capabilities
items.description: Define which information, tools, and intermediate results each stage needs, independently of a particular plugin name.

items.title: Test the handoffs and failure path
items.description: Verify that a failed tool or changed plugin produces a visible result and a clear decision about the next step.

en.seoDescription: Explore DeepSeek Harness’s plugin architecture and execution layer. Study capability composition, tool connections, and task handoffs before extending an agent workflow.

zh.seoTitle: DeepSeek Harness：插件、工具组合与 Agent 运行层
zh.description: 将 DeepSeek Harness 作为构建 Agent 工作流的参考，研究插件架构如何区分模型访问、工具与任务能力，再结合 Floatboat 中的工作需求评估可复用的扩展和组合方式。
overview: DeepSeek Harness 也称 dsh，是 DeepSeek 开发的开源 Agent Harness。它提供模型交互周围的运行系统，本身不是一个新模型。项目的核心设计是通过可组合的插件组织系统能力。
它对工作流设计的价值，在于把不同能力分成可组合的部分。Floatboat 用户可以先据此明确任务需要哪些工具、上下文和职责，再评估具体插件或运行层集成；参考架构本身不代表已经具备现成的 Floatboat 连接。
DeepSeek 将该项目标为开发者预览，并说明可能出现不兼容变更。MIT 源码许可与模型服务访问、第三方依赖条款分开。选用时应按持续演进的平台理解，结合具体版本文档与工作区边界进行评估。
zh.capabilitiesTitle: 值得借鉴的工作流机制
zh.capabilitiesIntro: DeepSeek Harness 让独立能力通过输入输出形成组合。插件职责和版本兼容性会影响整条处理链，理解每一阶段负责什么，才能判断组合是否适合自己的周期性交付任务。

capabilities.title: 清晰划分任务能力
capabilities.description: 参考插件优先的架构，将模型访问、工具和工作流职责作为不同部分设计。

capabilities.title: 组合范围明确的流程
capabilities.description: 只评估任务真正需要的能力，不将庞大的插件目录直接视为已经可用的完整方案。

capabilities.title: 为扩展变化留出边界
capabilities.description: 把版本兼容性纳入工作流设计，避免运行层更新后任务行为在未经检查的情况下变化。

useCases.title: DeepSeek Harness的使用场景
useCases.description: 新闻摘要需要连接采集与转换，自定义工具还涉及凭据和调用边界。借鉴 DeepSeek Harness 时，可以先验证小型能力组合，用真实输入检查兼容性及失败行为，再考虑长期采用。

items.title: 模块化的信息处理流程
items.description: 新闻摘要可以拆分为采集、转换和审阅等能力。围绕已确认的公开来源、去重规则和摘要审阅要求，定义每个插件接收与返回的内容。当来源重复或摘要需要修正时，可以沿输入输出映射找到对应职责，而不是把整个流程视为一个黑箱。

items.title: 面向业务的工具连接
items.description: 工作流缺少某个外部工具时，将它的 API 文档与当前插件约定对照，明确允许执行的操作，并引用已批准的凭据来源。连接方案除了描述成功调用，还要说明认证边界和失败处理，避免将密钥本身写进设计或任务材料。

items.title: 可控的工作流实验
items.description: 预览阶段的运行时应先通过小规模能力组合验证。限定能力范围，提供代表性输入和可接受的失败行为，记录实际运行表现。根据这次实验判断是否已有足够证据用于周期性工作，或仍需暂缓采用，避免直接将探索结果当作稳定能力。

items.title: 评估扩展升级的影响
items.description: 插件版本变化可能影响其他能力依赖的输入输出，不只是安装步骤。更新组合前，将当前约定和代表行为与拟议版本比较，记录不兼容假设及下游需要的检查。保留预览运行时的变化风险，避免将升级当作无需重新验证的常规替换。

faq.question: DeepSeek Harness 是 DeepSeek 官方项目吗？
faq.answer: 是。项目位于 deepseek-ai 组织，README 明确说明由 DeepSeek AI 开发。应以该仓库为准，不能把名称相似的社区分支自动视为官方项目。

faq.question: “一切皆插件”在这里是什么意思？
faq.answer: 这是项目基于 Cordis 的组合方式。运行层通过插件组织能力，实际工具与行为仍取决于会话启用了哪些插件及其配置，而不是默认拥有一切功能。

faq.question: dsh 是一个独立 AI 模型吗？
faq.answer: 不是。dsh 是运行层及其应用入口；模型推理由会话配置的服务提供，其凭证、可用性和商业条款应单独确认。

faq.question: 当前项目接口是否稳定？
faq.answer: 官方 README 将其标为开发者预览，并明确预期不兼容变更。应固定并评估实际使用的版本，不能假设扩展跨版本无需调整。

faq.question: MIT 许可是否覆盖接入的模型和服务？
faq.answer: MIT 适用于项目源码。模型 API、外部服务和第三方组件仍适用各自条款、费用和运行要求。

faq.question: 借鉴这些机制是否需要更换工作工具？
faq.answer: 不需要。可以先将 DeepSeek Harness 作为任务结构、工具边界和结果审阅的设计参考，在已有工作流中验证思路。软件复用是另一项选择，需要核对兼容性、权限与许可；借鉴设计思路不会自动完成软件与 Floatboat 的连接。

prerequisites.title: 核对 DeepSeek Harness 扩展条件
prerequisites.description: 不同 Harness 扩展可能依赖不同凭据、版本和运行环境。以下条件针对实际计划组合的能力核对，而不是准备一套泛化插件环境后，就默认所有连接具有相同执行要求。

items.title: 核对候选组合
items.description: 针对真正需要的扩展检查能力边界、凭证要求与版本兼容性。

howTo.title: 用 DeepSeek Harness 设计能力链
howTo.description: 能力链需要对应真实处理阶段，插件数量本身并不说明流程完整。划分职责并核对兼容性后，用代表输入检查交接和失败行为，再决定是否扩大组合或用于周期性交付。

items.title: 列出任务所需能力
items.description: 先明确各阶段需要的信息、工具和中间结果，不从插件名称倒推任务。

items.title: 测试交接与失败路径
items.description: 确认工具失败或插件变化时能够暴露问题，并明确后续如何处理。

zh.seoDescription: 了解 DeepSeek Harness 的插件架构与执行层，研究能力组合、工具连接和任务交接机制，再判断如何扩展自己的 Agent 工作流；运行环境与模型服务仍需分别配置。

en.seoTitle: DSH Superagent: GitHub Task Routing and Agent Delivery
en.description: Explore DeepSeek’s research prototype for turning authorized GitHub and Feishu requests into coding tasks. Study task routing, scoped execution, and reviewable delivery for your own agent workflows.
overview: DSH Superagent Prototype is a proactive coding agent published in DeepSeek’s official GitHub organization. It runs as a DeepSeek Harness bundle for one GitHub repository, with optional Feishu input. Authorized requests become tasks that execute in their own sessions and working directories, then return results to the original conversation.

Its useful workflow patterns include evaluating incoming requests, keeping each task within an assigned scope, and following discussion without treating every message as new authority. The web panel prioritizes work needing a person and also exposes history and operational health.

The MIT-licensed repository is research code, explicitly described as not an official DeepSeek product or production-ready software. Its published implementation differs from the internal version and the accompanying design article; some ideas discussed there remain unimplemented.
en.capabilitiesTitle: How Requests Become Agent Work
en.capabilitiesIntro: DSH connects an accountable request source with a bounded task and a result returned to the work's starting point. Compare those mechanisms when designing repository collaboration, keeping authorization and traceable delivery separate from simply receiving a message.

capabilities.title: Requests with an accountable source
capabilities.description: GitHub and optional Feishu events enter a policy-controlled routing process. Allowed senders, receiving scope, and team rules determine whether a request can become work.

capabilities.title: A scope for each task
capabilities.description: Accepted work becomes a Ticket with a Mandate defining its authority. Its executor uses a dedicated session and directory while subscribed conversations provide continuing context.

capabilities.title: Results where the work started
capabilities.description: The agent can reply in the original conversation and open pull requests. A panel brings review, blocked work, and other items needing human attention into view.

useCases.title: Use Cases for DSH Superagent Prototype
useCases.description: Maintenance requests, review follow-ups, and message-triggered work depend on a traceable task identity. Explore DSH's request-to-draft-PR handoff while keeping requester permissions, original scope, and result-return destinations explicit in your own workflow design.

items.title: Repository maintenance requests
items.description: Repository maintenance can follow a traceable request-to-ticket-to-draft-PR flow. Bound the coding request, permitted files, and acceptance conditions before work begins, and attach verification evidence to the proposed change. This makes the result inspectable without treating a draft pull request as an approved modification.

items.title: Follow-up after a review
items.description: Review feedback should stay attached to the task and authorization it concerns. Preserve the original scope when planning a continuation, and route unrelated requests into separate work instead of silently enlarging the assignment. The handoff should show which comments are being addressed and which require a new decision.

items.title: Team messages with a clear outcome
items.description: A message-triggered workflow needs approved channels, permitted requesters, and a clear destination for results. Define the trigger, authorization, assignment, and return path before borrowing that handoff pattern for work organized in Floatboat. Check connection requirements separately rather than assuming the channel is already integrated.

items.title: Review execution boundaries before enabling work
items.description: The router and worker environment should be assessed alongside requester rules and inferred-task handling. Read the current runtime prerequisites and identify which account, repository, and operating-system permissions the prototype would use. Keep observation settings, execution authorization, and machine isolation distinct, then decide which bounded experiment is acceptable before allowing the system to act on real repository requests.

en.articleTitle: From GitHub Requests to Agent Workflows
en.articleDescription: Trace a request through authorization, task execution, and delivery, then decide which mechanisms fit your own workflow.

faq.question: Is DSH Superagent a DeepSeek model?
faq.answer: It is agent application code running on DeepSeek Harness. A separately configured model provider supplies inference; the project itself is not model weights or a model API subscription.

faq.question: How does it differ from DeepSeek Harness?
faq.answer: Harness provides the surrounding agent runtime and extension system. Superagent is a bundle built on that runtime to coordinate requests, tasks, sessions, and delivery for a repository.

faq.question: Does it need Feishu or support every GitHub deployment?
faq.answer: Feishu is optional. The documented scope is one github.com repository per deployment; GitHub Enterprise Server is unsupported. The agent needs a dedicated GitHub user with write access, rather than a GitHub App.

faq.question: Does observe mode stop every task from running?
faq.answer: No. It evaluates inferred candidates and records positive assessments without accepting them. Explicit requests work in every mode; automatic acceptance of inferred work requires auto mode and matching rules.

faq.question: Are workers isolated from the rest of my computer?
faq.answer: No security sandbox is provided by the separate task directories or account wrappers. The documented presets run with full OS-user access, so the deployment guide recommends a dedicated OS account containing only the agent credentials.

faq.question: Does MIT make it production-ready or include free inference?
faq.answer: MIT covers the source code. Model services and machine operation have separate costs and terms. The README identifies the software as a research prototype, with differences from its internal implementation and some unimplemented design ideas.

prerequisites.title: Prepare the DSH Superagent runtime
prerequisites.description: Running the prototype requires a compatible Harness environment, configured model access, and a dedicated repository identity. Review those conditions alongside operating-system permissions: separate sessions and credential wrappers do not themselves provide a sandbox for router or worker activity.

items.title: Prepare the runtime and agent identity
items.description: Use a supported Harness version, a configured model provider, and the documented command-line dependencies. One deployment serves one github.com repository through a dedicated GitHub user account.

items.title: Separate machine permissions
items.description: The documented router and worker presets run with full access as the operating-system user. Separate sessions and credential wrappers are not a sandbox; use a dedicated OS account for isolation.

howTo.title: Inspect DSH Superagent’s task decisions
howTo.description: Observation helps assess inferred tasks before automatic acceptance is enabled, but explicit requests can still execute in observe mode. Review the steps with that distinction intact, checking permissions and task records rather than treating the mode as a universal execution block.

items.title: Inspect inferred work first
items.description: The default observe mode records inferred tasks it would accept without starting them; explicit requests still execute. Review decisions before enabling automatic acceptance under written rules.

en.seoDescription: Examine DSH Superagent Prototype’s GitHub and optional Feishu request flow, scoped coding execution, and result delivery. Treat it as a research prototype, not a hosted service.

zh.seoTitle: DSH Superagent：GitHub 任务路由与 Agent 结果交付
zh.description: 了解 DeepSeek 的主动编程 Agent 研究原型，如何将 GitHub 与飞书中的授权请求转为任务。参考任务路由、范围管理和结果交付机制，构建或优化自己的 Agent 工作流。
zh.kind: 编程 Agent 研究原型
overview: DSH Superagent Prototype 是 DeepSeek 官方 GitHub 组织发布的主动编程 Agent 研究原型。它作为 DeepSeek Harness 的扩展包运行，面向单个 GitHub 仓库，也可接收飞书消息；授权请求会转为任务，在独立会话和工作目录中执行，再把结果送回原讨论。
值得借鉴的机制包括请求评估、任务范围管理，以及跟进讨论时区分上下文与新增授权。网页面板优先呈现需要人工处理的事项，同时提供历史记录和运行健康信息，帮助团队跟踪任务与结果。
仓库采用 MIT 许可，README 明确其并非正式 DeepSeek 产品，也不属于生产就绪软件。公开实现与内部版本、配套设计文章并不完全一致，文章中的部分设计尚未实现，采用时应以实际代码和文档为准。
zh.capabilitiesTitle: 从团队请求到 Agent 任务
zh.capabilitiesIntro: 消息进入 DSH 后，还需要对应可问责的来源、明确范围和结果回传位置。这些机制使仓库任务能够追溯，收到请求本身则不能代替授权判断，也不能证明结果已经被接受。

capabilities.title: 有来源的任务请求
capabilities.description: GitHub 与可选飞书事件进入受策略约束的路由流程。允许的请求者、消息接收范围与团队规则，共同决定一条请求能否转为工作。

capabilities.title: 有范围的独立执行
capabilities.description: 已接受的工作会建立 Ticket，并通过 Mandate 记录授权范围。执行者使用独立会话和目录，订阅讨论则为后续步骤补充上下文。

capabilities.title: 回到原讨论的交付
capabilities.description: Agent 可以在原会话中回复结果并创建 Pull Request。面板汇集待审阅、受阻及其他需要人工关注的事项，方便继续推进任务。

useCases.title: DSH Superagent Prototype的使用场景
useCases.description: 仓库维护和审阅跟进需要回到同一任务，消息触发还要明确谁有权提出请求。DSH 的交接方式可用于设计可追踪的请求链，同时保留原范围、结果回传位置及单独核验的连接条件。

items.title: 处理仓库维护请求
items.description: 仓库维护可以按请求、任务单和草稿 PR 的链路组织。开始前限定编码需求、允许修改的文件和验收条件，交付时将验证证据附到拟议变更上。这样既方便追溯和审阅结果，也不会把生成草稿 PR 误当作变更已经获准。

items.title: 跟进评审与后续反馈
items.description: 审阅反馈应关联到对应任务及原始授权。安排后续处理时保留已有范围，将无关需求单独分流，不在原任务中静默扩大工作。交接说明应让人看清本轮正在处理哪些评论，以及哪些新要求还需要另外决定。

items.title: 把团队消息变为交付目标
items.description: 由消息触发的工作流，需要明确允许的频道、请求人和结果返回位置。先定义触发、授权、任务分配和交付链路，再将这种交接方式借鉴到 Floatboat 中组织的工作。连接要求应独立核验，不能因为流程相似就假定已有内置集成。

items.title: 启用任务前审阅执行边界
items.description: 路由和工作进程的环境，需要与请求者规则及推断任务处理一起检查。依据当前运行前提，明确原型使用哪个账号、仓库和操作系统权限。将观察设置、执行授权及机器隔离分开，再决定可以接受哪种限定实验，之后才考虑真实仓库请求。

zh.articleTitle: GitHub 请求如何变成 Agent 工作流
zh.articleDescription: 跟随一次请求理解授权、任务执行与交付，再判断哪些机制适合自己的工作方式。

faq.question: DSH Superagent 是 DeepSeek 模型吗？
faq.answer: 它是在 DeepSeek Harness 上运行的 Agent 应用代码，推理由另行配置的模型服务提供。项目本身不是模型权重，也不包含模型 API 订阅。

faq.question: 它与 DeepSeek Harness 有什么区别？
faq.answer: Harness 提供 Agent 运行环境与扩展机制；Superagent 是基于它构建的扩展包，负责仓库中的请求接收、任务管理、会话执行与结果交付。

faq.question: 必须接入飞书吗，支持所有 GitHub 环境吗？
faq.answer: 飞书是可选入口。当前文档限定一次部署面向一个 github.com 仓库，不支持 GitHub Enterprise Server。执行身份需要具有仓库写权限的专用 GitHub 用户账号，而非 GitHub App。

faq.question: observe 模式会阻止全部任务执行吗？
faq.answer: 不会。它会评估推断任务，并记录本来会接受的结果，但不真正接受这些任务。显式请求在所有模式下仍可执行；推断任务自动接受需要启用 auto 模式并匹配规则。

faq.question: 独立工作目录能隔离我的电脑吗？
faq.answer: 不能。独立任务目录和账号包装不构成安全沙箱。文档中的预设拥有操作系统用户的完整执行权限，因此部署指南建议使用只放置 Agent 凭据的专用操作系统账号。

faq.question: MIT 是否意味着已经成熟并且推理免费？
faq.answer: MIT 适用于源码，模型服务和机器运行另有费用与条款。README 将其定位为研究原型，公开版与内部实现存在差异，设计文章中的部分方案也尚未实现。

prerequisites.title: 准备 DSH Superagent 运行环境
prerequisites.description: 运行原型需要兼容 Harness 环境、模型访问和专用仓库身份。以下条件同时涉及操作系统权限；独立会话与凭据包装本身不构成沙箱，不能据此假定路由或工作进程已被隔离。

items.title: 准备运行环境和 Agent 身份
items.description: 需要受支持的 Harness 版本、已配置的模型服务和文档列出的命令行依赖。一次部署面向一个 github.com 仓库，通过专用 GitHub 用户账号执行操作。

items.title: 划清机器与账号权限
items.description: 文档中的路由与工作预设以操作系统用户身份拥有完整执行权限。独立会话和凭据包装并非沙箱；需要隔离时，应使用专用操作系统账号。

howTo.title: 检查 DSH Superagent 的任务判断
howTo.description: 观察记录可帮助判断推断任务是否适合自动接受，但 observe 模式中的明确请求仍可能执行。核对权限和任务记录时必须保留这个区别，不能把该模式当作全面阻止执行的开关。

items.title: 先检查推断任务的判断
items.description: 默认 observe 模式只记录本来会接受的推断任务，显式请求仍可执行。先检查决策记录，再根据书面规则启用推断任务的自动接受。

zh.seoDescription: 查看 DSH Superagent Prototype 的 GitHub 与可选飞书请求流程，了解任务路由、授权范围、编程执行和结果回传。它是研究原型，部署与运行条件需按上游说明核对。

en.seoTitle: Pi Agent Harness: Extensions, Runtime Libraries, and Task Design
en.description: Study Pi’s minimal agent core, extension packages, and reusable libraries to shape your own workflows. Compare where task instructions are enough, where runtime customization helps, and which execution boundaries your environment must provide.
overview: Pi explicitly describes itself as a minimal, extensible agent harness. The project combines an interactive coding agent with supporting libraries for model access, agent execution, conversation state, and terminal interfaces. It is both a usable tool and a collection of building blocks.

Pi is useful when designing a workflow that needs a small core with selective additions. In Floatboat-related work, use it to distinguish a reusable task instruction from a new tool or runtime behavior. Some improvements only need better Skills; others justify evaluating an extension or library.

The current repository is earendil-works/pi, following the earlier badlogic/pi-mono location, and uses MIT. Pi also explicitly says it has no built-in permission system restricting filesystem, process, network, or credential access. Hosting it safely requires the surrounding environment to provide the boundaries you need.
en.capabilitiesTitle: Workflow Mechanisms to Learn From
en.capabilitiesIntro: Pi provides a small execution core alongside separate instruction, extension, and library responsibilities. Compare those layers before adding functionality, so a missing task method is not automatically treated as a need for another executable runtime component.

capabilities.title: A small execution core
capabilities.description: Study the minimal harness to identify the state and tool feedback your workflow really needs before adding higher-level features.

capabilities.title: Distinct extension layers
capabilities.description: Separate instructions, prompts, themes, and executable extensions so each workflow change is made at the right layer.

capabilities.title: Reusable runtime components
capabilities.description: Evaluate the provider API, agent core, and conversation libraries independently when building a custom workflow component.

useCases.title: Use Cases for Pi
useCases.description: A small task loop, an unreliable Skill, and a custom runtime component need different extension decisions. Compare Pi's instruction and library boundaries before deciding whether clearer task knowledge or additional executable behavior would address the gap.

items.title: A lightweight task loop
items.description: A lightweight reporting loop can start with one objective, readable files, and a small permitted tool set. Use Pi's focused structure to describe how context leads to tool use and result review. Test a reproducible sample output before introducing a larger collection of runtime features.

items.title: Improving a reusable Skill
items.description: When a reusable Skill repeatedly fails, compare its current instructions and resources with the behavior you expect. Correct those gaps and test counterexamples before introducing another executable extension. The review should identify which instruction changes are sufficient and whether any runtime capability is still missing.

items.title: A custom agent component
items.description: A business workflow with its own model interface or execution boundaries can use Pi's library structure as a design reference. Map the required provider behavior and business interfaces to those responsibilities, then identify the adapters you would need. Keep the component design grounded in the environment you actually own.

items.title: Define the host's permission policy
items.description: A minimal agent core does not determine which files, processes, or services it may access in your environment. Use Pi's lack of a built-in permission system as an explicit design constraint when planning the host. Document allowed operations and review points, then test representative boundaries without mistaking package separation or clear instructions for enforced execution controls.

faq.question: Is Pi officially described as a harness?
faq.answer: Yes. The README explicitly calls Pi a minimal, extensible agent harness. It also contains a coding CLI and reusable libraries, so the repository covers more than one user-facing interface.

faq.question: Why do old links use badlogic/pi-mono?
faq.answer: That was the earlier repository address. It currently redirects to earendil-works/pi. Use the current upstream for ownership and documentation, and check older package references before reusing them.

faq.question: Does Pi include a built-in permission sandbox?
faq.answer: The README says Pi has no built-in permission system for restricting filesystem, process, network, or credential access. Required containment must come from the environment, not from an assumption that every harness provides it.

faq.question: Are subagents and plan mode enabled by default?
faq.answer: The project deliberately leaves those features out of its core defaults. Extensions or packages may supply them, but their presence and behavior must be checked for the particular setup.

faq.question: What is the difference between a Skill and an extension?
faq.answer: A Skill supplies reusable task instructions and resources. An extension changes or extends the running tool through the extension mechanism. They can work together, but their execution and trust boundaries differ.

faq.question: Must I switch products to use these workflow ideas?
faq.answer: No. You can first use Pi as a reference for task structure, tool boundaries, and result review in your existing workflow. Reusing software is a separate choice that requires compatibility, permissions, and license checks; applying the design ideas does not automatically connect the software to Floatboat.

prerequisites.title: Define Pi’s host permissions
prerequisites.description: Pi does not provide a built-in permission system for the work it hosts. Define file, process, network, and credential access in the surrounding environment before testing an extension, keeping the host's actual execution boundary separate from its package structure.

items.title: Set the execution boundary
items.description: Plan file, process, network, and credential access in the host environment; Pi does not supply a built-in permission system.

howTo.title: Choose and test a Pi extension
howTo.description: Extending Pi begins by identifying which layer the task actually needs. Test one instruction or runtime extension with representative material before combining more packages, and use the observed behavior to decide whether the additional execution surface is justified.

items.title: Choose the extension layer
items.description: Identify whether the gap is in instructions, available tools, conversation state, or the surrounding interface.

items.title: Evaluate the smallest addition
items.description: Validate one package or component against a representative task before combining several additions.

en.seoDescription: Study Pi’s minimal agent core, Skills, extensions, and runtime libraries. Choose the level of customization your workflow needs without assuming the host supplies every tool.

zh.seoTitle: Pi Agent Harness：扩展、运行基础库与任务设计
zh.description: 参考 Pi 的精简 Agent 核心、扩展包与基础库，设计适合自己的工作流。区分哪些问题可以通过任务说明解决，哪些需要运行层定制，以及执行环境应提供哪些边界。
overview: Pi 明确将自己定位为精简、可扩展的 Agent Harness。项目把交互式编程 Agent 与模型访问、Agent 执行、对话状态和终端界面等基础库放在一起，既能作为工具使用，也能为其他应用提供构建模块。
Pi 适合作为“精简核心、按需增加能力”的设计参考。围绕 Floatboat 的工作，可以用它区分可复用任务说明、新工具和运行层行为：部分优化只需更好的 Skills，另一些才值得评估扩展或基础库。
当前仓库为 earendil-works/pi，原地址为 badlogic/pi-mono，采用 MIT 许可。项目也明确说明自身没有限制文件、进程、网络和凭证访问的内置权限系统；所需隔离边界应由实际运行环境提供。
zh.capabilitiesTitle: 值得借鉴的工作流机制
zh.capabilitiesIntro: Pi 的精简核心周围保留了指令、扩展和库的不同职责。任务方法不清楚时，优先确认是否需要完善知识，而不是直接增加可执行组件，让真正的运行缺口与内容问题分开处理。

capabilities.title: 精简执行核心
capabilities.description: 参考精简 harness，先确定流程真正需要的状态和工具反馈，再增加上层功能。

capabilities.title: 不同层次的扩展
capabilities.description: 区分指令、提示、主题和可执行扩展，让每种工作流调整发生在合适的层次。

capabilities.title: 可复用运行组件
capabilities.description: 构建特定流程组件时，可以分别评估模型接口、Agent 核心和对话基础库。

useCases.title: Pi的使用场景
useCases.description: 有的任务只需更清楚的 Skill，有的才需要自定义模型或执行接口。Pi 的分层提供了比较这些选择的参考，可以从轻量循环入手验证缺口，再决定是否增加运行组件。

items.title: 轻量任务循环
items.description: 轻量报告流程可以从一个目标、可读取的文件和少量允许使用的工具开始。参考 Pi 的精简结构，说明上下文如何进入工具调用，以及结果如何被审阅。先验证一个可复现的输出样例，再判断是否需要增加更多运行时功能。

items.title: 优化可复用 Skill
items.description: 可复用 Skill 反复出现问题时，先对照预期行为检查现有指令与参考资料。修正缺口后使用反例验证，再判断是否仍需要新增可执行扩展。审阅结果应区分能够通过内容调整解决的问题，以及确实缺少运行时能力的部分。

items.title: 定制 Agent 组件
items.description: 业务工作流需要自有模型接口或执行边界时，可以参考 Pi 的库职责进行设计。将模型提供方约束、业务接口和执行要求逐项对应，识别必须补充的适配器。组件方案应围绕实际掌握的环境展开，而不是直接照搬另一套运行方式。

items.title: 为宿主定义权限策略
items.description: 精简 Agent 核心并不能决定它在当前环境可以访问哪些文件、进程或服务。规划宿主时，需要将 Pi 不提供内置权限系统作为明确约束。记录允许操作和审阅节点，再测试代表性边界，不把包的分层或指令清楚误当成已经强制执行的控制。

faq.question: Pi 官方是否将自己称为 harness？
faq.answer: 是。README 明确将 Pi 称为精简、可扩展的 Agent Harness，同时提供编程 CLI 和可复用基础库，范围不止一个终端界面。

faq.question: 为什么旧资料使用 badlogic/pi-mono？
faq.answer: 那是旧仓库地址，目前会转向 earendil-works/pi。归属与文档应以当前上游为准，复用旧资料前也要确认包名和接口是否变化。

faq.question: Pi 是否自带权限沙箱？
faq.answer: README 说明 Pi 没有用于限制文件、进程、网络和凭证访问的内置权限系统。需要的隔离应由环境提供，不能假定所有 harness 都自带沙箱。

faq.question: 子 Agent 和规划模式默认就有吗？
faq.answer: 项目有意不将这类能力作为核心默认功能。扩展或包可以补充，是否可用取决于所选扩展、包和会话配置。

faq.question: Skill 与扩展在 Pi 中有什么区别？
faq.answer: Skill 提供可复用的任务说明与资料，扩展则通过扩展机制改变或增加工具行为。两者可以配合，但执行方式与信任边界不同。

faq.question: 借鉴这些机制是否需要更换工作工具？
faq.answer: 不需要。可以先将 Pi 作为任务结构、工具边界和结果审阅的设计参考，在已有工作流中验证思路。软件复用是另一项选择，需要核对兼容性、权限与许可；借鉴设计思路不会自动完成软件与 Floatboat 的连接。

prerequisites.title: 明确 Pi 宿主权限
prerequisites.description: Pi 不为所承载工作提供内置权限系统。以下条件需要在外围环境中明确文件、进程、网络和凭据访问，再测试扩展；包结构的分层不能代替宿主实际执行边界。

items.title: 设置执行边界
items.description: 在宿主环境中规划文件、进程、网络与凭证访问；Pi 没有内置权限限制系统。

howTo.title: 选择并验证 Pi 扩展
howTo.description: 扩展应先补足任务缺口，而不是增加包的数量。确认需要调整指令还是运行层后，用代表材料验证单项能力，再评估进一步组合，使新增执行范围有实际需求和行为作为依据。

items.title: 选择改动层次
items.description: 确认不足来自任务说明、可用工具、对话状态还是交互界面。

items.title: 评估最小必要扩展
items.description: 先针对代表任务验证一个包或组件，再组合更多能力。

zh.seoDescription: 研究 Pi 的精简 Agent 核心、Skills、扩展与运行基础库，按任务选择所需定制层级，了解模型、工具和宿主环境各自承担的职责，避免把扩展能力视为默认配置。

en.seoTitle: OpenCode: Coding-Agent Modes, Tool Feedback, and Review
en.description: Study OpenCode’s coding-agent workflow to improve how your own tasks move from investigation to changes and review. Use its interaction and extension design as references for development work organized in Floatboat.
overview: OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent published by Anomaly. It connects task conversations with repository tools. The model service supplies reasoning and generation, the execution environment handles files and commands, and the application coordinates the workflow.

For workflow design, OpenCode is a concrete implementation to study rather than a requirement to switch products. Its agent modes and interactive feedback can inform how you separate investigation from implementation, expose a change for review, and add task-specific integrations to your own environment.

The project source is MIT licensed. Model-provider accounts, subscription access, remote services, and community additions have separate requirements. The source can be inspected and adapted without implying that all associated hosted services are free or included.
en.capabilitiesTitle: Workflow Mechanisms to Learn From
en.capabilitiesIntro: OpenCode's modes, tool feedback, and extension interfaces address different parts of coding work. Compare how they separate investigation from modification, make results inspectable, and expose project-specific integrations without confusing the agent application with its model service.

capabilities.title: Separate task modes
capabilities.description: Study the division of agent responsibilities when deciding which workflow stages should inspect, plan, or change a repository.

capabilities.title: Expose useful feedback
capabilities.description: Use the interactive workflow as a reference for showing progress and tool results where a person can make an informed decision.

capabilities.title: Evaluate integrations by task
capabilities.description: Inspect an integration’s tools and maintainer before adapting the pattern to the development workflow you actually need.

useCases.title: Use Cases for OpenCode
useCases.description: Repository investigation, code review, and development-tool connections require different permissions and outputs. Explore how OpenCode's workflow can inform a read-only discovery stage, an inspectable change pipeline, and bounded extension tests for your own project.

items.title: A repository investigation stage
items.description: Before implementing a repository feature, define what the agent must learn about the relevant files, routes, and data entry points. Keep the investigation read-only while collecting constraints and unresolved decisions. Its findings should tell the implementation stage where to work and which questions still need an answer.

items.title: A reviewable change pipeline
items.description: A proposed code change should remain distinct from its acceptance. Present the diff with relevant test results and the context the responsible reviewer needs, then make acceptance an explicit step. This gives the workflow an inspectable change pipeline rather than treating generated code as finished work.

items.title: A task-specific development tool
items.description: A project's existing checks or external development systems may need a task-specific extension. Compare the documented interfaces with the available commands, API requirements, and permitted access. Assess compatibility first, then run one bounded tool-call test to establish what the proposed connection can actually do.

items.title: Separate model access from tool permissions
items.description: Choosing a model provider and granting an agent access to repository tools solve different problems. Compare OpenCode's model-service boundary with the environment where commands and edits occur, using your task's actual access requirements. Prepare a plan that states both sets of prerequisites so an authenticated model connection is not treated as approval for every available tool action.

faq.question: Is OpenCode a model provider?
faq.answer: OpenCode is a coding-agent application that provides the interface and execution workflow. The model used by a session depends on its provider configuration; the application and model service have different responsibilities.

faq.question: Should OpenCode be called a Skill?
faq.answer: No. It is an independent coding-agent project. Skills or other instructions can form part of an agent workflow, but they do not replace the application that runs the workflow.

faq.question: Who publishes the official repository?
faq.answer: The repository is anomalyco/opencode, under Anomaly’s GitHub organization. Community integrations and similarly named projects should be checked separately rather than attributed to Anomaly automatically.

faq.question: Are planning and building the same mode?
faq.answer: The official project documents different agent modes for different responsibilities. Read the selected mode’s behavior and permissions before assuming a planning session can or should make changes.

faq.question: Does MIT include a free model subscription?
faq.answer: No. It covers the application source. Provider accounts, model usage, commercial subscriptions, and external integrations have their own conditions and costs.

faq.question: Must I switch products to use these workflow ideas?
faq.answer: No. You can first use OpenCode as a reference for task structure, tool boundaries, and result review in your existing workflow. Reusing software is a separate choice that requires compatibility, permissions, and license checks; applying the design ideas does not automatically connect the software to Floatboat.

howTo.title: Build a reviewable OpenCode handoff
howTo.description: A reviewable OpenCode-inspired workflow needs a clear result from each stage. Define the investigation handoff and tool boundaries before implementation, then use diffs and verification evidence to decide whether the proposed change should be accepted in your repository.

items.title: Describe the desired handoff
items.description: Write down what investigation must deliver before planning or implementation can safely continue.

items.title: Limit available actions
items.description: Match tool access and the active mode to each stage rather than giving every step the same ability to change files.

items.title: Check the result and feedback
items.description: Evaluate whether the workflow makes errors visible and gives the user enough evidence to accept or revise the change.

en.seoDescription: Explore OpenCode’s task modes and execution feedback for repository investigation, implementation, and review. Keep the coding-agent runtime separate from model-service choices.

zh.seoTitle: OpenCode：编程 Agent 模式、工具反馈与审阅流程
zh.description: 参考 OpenCode 的编程 Agent 工作方式，优化自己的任务如何从代码理解进入修改与审阅。围绕 Floatboat 中的开发工作，研究交互、任务模式和扩展机制可以带来的流程改进。
overview: OpenCode 是 Anomaly 发布的开源 AI 编程 Agent，将任务对话与仓库中的开发工具连接起来。模型服务提供生成与推理能力，执行环境负责文件访问和命令运行，应用则组织这些环节之间的协作。
在工作流设计中，OpenCode 提供了可以研究的具体实现，而不是要求用户更换产品。可以借鉴其 Agent 模式与交互反馈，区分理解与实施、呈现待审阅修改，并评估如何为自己的环境增加任务集成。
项目源码采用 MIT 许可。模型服务账号、订阅访问、远程服务和社区扩展各有独立要求。可以研究和修改源码，但不能据此认为全部相关托管服务均免费或包含在内。
zh.capabilitiesTitle: 值得借鉴的工作流机制
zh.capabilitiesIntro: 任务模式决定调查或修改的方式，工具反馈让过程可检查，扩展接口再连接项目需要的能力。理解 OpenCode 时，这些应用职责还需与模型服务分开，避免将一层能力推给另一层承担。

capabilities.title: 区分任务模式
capabilities.description: 研究 Agent 职责划分，确定流程中哪些阶段负责检查、规划或修改仓库。

capabilities.title: 呈现有用反馈
capabilities.description: 参考交互流程，在用户能够作出判断的位置呈现进度与工具结果。

capabilities.title: 按任务评估集成
capabilities.description: 在借鉴集成方式之前，检查工具范围与维护者，并对应到实际开发需求。

useCases.title: OpenCode的使用场景
useCases.description: 仓库调查应先交回可核对发现，代码修改应展示差异，开发工具连接则需要限定测试。OpenCode 的工作方式可以帮助设计这些环节，明确各阶段权限和输出，而不混淆执行与接受。

items.title: 代码调查阶段
items.description: 实施仓库功能前，先明确需要调查的文件、路由与数据入口。保持只读调查，整理真实约束和尚未确定的决定。调查结果应能够告诉实施环节应该在哪里修改、哪些问题仍需回答，避免在尚未理解代码时直接开始改动。

items.title: 可审阅的修改流程
items.description: 拟议代码变更与最终接受应分开处理。展示修改差异、相关测试结果和负责人审阅所需的上下文，再明确进入接受环节。这样形成的流程能够逐步检查变更，而不会因为代码已经生成就将任务视为完成。

items.title: 面向任务的开发工具
items.description: 项目已有检查命令或外部开发系统可能需要专用扩展。将公开接口与现有命令、API 要求和允许的访问范围进行比较，先评估兼容性，再执行一次范围受限的工具调用测试，用实际结果说明拟议连接能够处理什么。

items.title: 分开核对模型与工具权限
items.description: 选择模型提供方和允许 Agent 使用仓库工具，是两类不同问题。结合任务实际访问要求，对照 OpenCode 的模型服务边界及命令、编辑发生的环境。方案同时写明两类前提，不把模型连接已经认证理解为所有可用工具动作都已获准。

faq.question: OpenCode 是模型提供商吗？
faq.answer: OpenCode 是编程 Agent 应用，负责交互与执行工作流。具体模型由会话配置决定，应用与模型服务分别承担不同职责。

faq.question: OpenCode 应归为 Skill 吗？
faq.answer: 不应。它是独立编程 Agent 项目；Skills 等任务说明可以参与工作流，但不能代替运行工作流的应用本身。

faq.question: 官方仓库由谁发布？
faq.answer: 官方仓库为 Anomaly GitHub 组织下的 anomalyco/opencode。社区集成和同名项目需要另行核实，不能自动归属于 Anomaly。

faq.question: 规划和实施是否属于同一种模式？
faq.answer: 官方项目为不同职责介绍了不同 Agent 模式。应先了解所选模式的行为和权限，再判断会话是否应该修改内容。

faq.question: MIT 许可包含免费模型订阅吗？
faq.answer: 不包含。MIT 许可覆盖应用源码，模型账号、调用、商业订阅和外部集成分别适用自身条件与费用。

faq.question: 借鉴这些机制是否需要更换工作工具？
faq.answer: 不需要。可以先将 OpenCode 作为任务结构、工具边界和结果审阅的设计参考，在已有工作流中验证思路。软件复用是另一项选择，需要核对兼容性、权限与许可；借鉴设计思路不会自动完成软件与 Floatboat 的连接。

howTo.title: 构建可审阅的 OpenCode 交接
howTo.description: 调查、修改和接受变更需要不同证据。先约定只读阶段交回的结果及工具范围，再依据实现差异和验证记录决定是否接纳代码，使执行成功不会直接替代仓库审阅。

items.title: 描述阶段交接
items.description: 明确调查阶段必须交付什么，后续规划或实施才有足够依据。

items.title: 限定可用操作
items.description: 按阶段匹配工具访问和工作模式，而非让每一步都拥有同样的修改能力。

items.title: 检查结果与反馈
items.description: 评估流程能否暴露错误，并为用户接受或修订修改提供足够证据。

zh.seoDescription: 了解 OpenCode 的任务模式与工具反馈，研究仓库调查、修改实施和结果审阅如何衔接。区分编程 Agent 运行层与模型服务，为自己的开发流程选择适合的执行机制。

en.seoTitle: Hermes Agent: Persistent Memory, Skills, and Scheduled Work
en.description: Use Hermes Agent as a reference for workflows that continue across sessions. Study how memory, procedural Skills, tool connections, and scheduling can help organize reusable task knowledge and recurring work in your own environment.
overview: Hermes Agent is an open-source agent system from Nous Research. Its official documentation brings together persistent memory, reusable Skills, tools, context files, and scheduling. These capabilities place it in the category of an independent agent application rather than a single prompt or Skill.

The value for a Floatboat user is in deciding what a continuing workflow needs to retain: facts, preferences, decisions, or a procedure. Hermes provides a reference for separating those concerns and combining them with tools and schedules. The design still needs task-specific review and an independently verified integration path.

Hermes also documents MCP integrations, execution controls, and scheduled tasks. Each connected tool or delivery channel adds its own setup and permissions. The MIT license covers the source, while models, remote systems, and hosted services remain separate choices.
en.capabilitiesTitle: Workflow Mechanisms to Learn From
en.capabilitiesIntro: Hermes Agent offers reference points for retained context, reusable procedures, and task continuity over time. Compare those responsibilities before storing information, so knowledge that should be maintained separately does not become an undifferentiated archive of every past conversation.

capabilities.title: Retain the right context
capabilities.description: Study persistent memory when a workflow needs information from earlier sessions, with a way to correct or retire it.

capabilities.title: Keep procedures separate
capabilities.description: Use procedural Skills as a reference for storing how a task should be done separately from facts about a particular user or project.

capabilities.title: Connect continuity and timing
capabilities.description: Evaluate how recurring work should receive context, use tools, and deliver a result at a planned time.

useCases.title: Use Cases for Hermes Agent
useCases.description: Recurring briefs, reusable methods, and resumed tasks need different memory boundaries. Use Hermes Agent as a reference for retaining source freshness and essential decisions while defining how task knowledge is reviewed, updated, and separated from unrelated history.

items.title: A recurring research brief
items.description: A recurring research brief needs fresh sources without losing its original scope. Define how weekly additions enter the workflow, how their freshness is marked, and how citations remain attached to the digest. Reusable rules should preserve the output requirements while allowing each period's findings to differ.

items.title: A reusable working method
items.description: A proven working method can become task knowledge only when its assumptions and ownership are clear. Review the procedure against counterexamples, prepare a memory or Skill draft, and define who updates it when conditions change. Stored knowledge should remain reviewable rather than accumulating obsolete instructions indefinitely.

items.title: A task resumed later
items.description: Resuming a task later requires the decisions and evidence that determine the next action. Extract those essentials from the paused state and leave unrelated conversation history out. A concise continuation record should let the next session understand what is settled, what remains open, and where the supporting evidence lives.

items.title: Revisit knowledge after its sources change
items.description: A reusable method may depend on a source, condition, or decision that is no longer current. Compare the retained task knowledge with the changed material and identify which assumptions need review. Use Hermes Agent as a reference for continuity, while defining who accepts updates and how obsolete guidance is distinguished from the version that future tasks should follow.

faq.question: How is Hermes Agent different from a Skill collection?
faq.answer: Hermes is the running agent system. Skills are one way it represents reusable task knowledge alongside memory, tools, and scheduling. A collection of instructions alone does not supply that surrounding application.

faq.question: Is persistent memory the same as chat history?
faq.answer: No. The project documents persistent memory and conversation context as distinct concerns. When evaluating it, inspect what is stored, how it is reused, and how you can correct or remove information.

faq.question: Does saving a Skill make it trustworthy?
faq.answer: No. Reusable procedures can contain outdated assumptions or task-specific mistakes. Review their source, dependencies, and results before treating them as a reliable routine.

faq.question: Can Hermes connect to MCP tools?
faq.answer: The official documentation includes MCP integration. The actual services available depend on configured servers, credentials, and access policies; a supported protocol does not grant access to every service.

faq.question: Must I switch products to use these workflow ideas?
faq.answer: No. You can first use Hermes Agent as a reference for task structure, tool boundaries, and result review in your existing workflow. Reusing software is a separate choice that requires compatibility, permissions, and license checks; applying the design ideas does not automatically connect the software to Floatboat.

faq.question: Who maintains Hermes Agent and its source license?
faq.answer: The official repository is published by Nous Research and identifies the source license as MIT. Connected model services and external systems have their own access and commercial conditions.

howTo.title: Maintain knowledge across Hermes Agent runs
howTo.description: Reusable task knowledge needs an owner and an update rule as well as a place to persist. Separate it from temporary session context, then assess repeated tasks against fresh evidence before deciding that the memory and continuity design is reliable.

items.title: Classify what should persist
items.description: Separate temporary context, durable facts, decisions, and procedures before adding a memory mechanism.

items.title: Define correction and delivery
items.description: Give stored knowledge an update process and recurring tasks an explicit schedule, output destination, and failure path.

items.title: Evaluate repeated runs
items.description: Check whether the workflow stays accurate as inputs change, rather than judging it from one successful run.

en.seoDescription: Inspect Hermes Agent’s memory, reusable Skills, tools, and scheduling. Consider how context continuity and stored procedures can support recurring work in your own system.

zh.seoTitle: Hermes Agent：持续记忆、Skills 与调度任务机制
zh.description: 参考 Hermes Agent 的记忆、程序性 Skills、工具连接与调度方式，设计能够跨会话继续推进的工作流，为自己的任务保留必要背景、沉淀方法并组织重复工作。
zh.kind: 持续工作 Agent 系统
overview: Hermes Agent 是 Nous Research 的开源 Agent 系统。官方文档将持久记忆、可复用 Skills、工具、上下文文件和调度能力组织在一起，因此它属于独立 Agent 应用，而非单个提示或 Skill。
对 Floatboat 用户而言，重点是决定持续工作流需要保留哪些事实、偏好、决策或流程。Hermes 为区分这些信息、再结合工具与调度提供了参考；实际设计仍需要任务审阅，并单独验证接入方式。
Hermes 还维护 MCP 集成、执行控制与定时任务说明。每种工具和交付渠道都有自己的配置与权限。MIT 许可适用于源码，模型、远程系统和托管服务仍是独立选择。
zh.capabilitiesTitle: 值得借鉴的工作流机制
zh.capabilitiesIntro: 上下文延续和方法复用并不需要保存完全相同的信息。Hermes Agent 为任务续接、知识维护及时间衔接提供参考，真正值得保留的内容需要有边界，而不是把全部对话堆成长期归档。

capabilities.title: 保留必要背景
capabilities.description: 流程需要引用此前会话的信息时，可以参考持久记忆，并设计纠正与失效处理。

capabilities.title: 单独维护任务方法
capabilities.description: 参考程序性 Skills，将任务应如何开展与具体用户、项目事实分开维护。

capabilities.title: 连接持续性与时间安排
capabilities.description: 研究重复工作如何获得背景资料、使用工具，并在约定时间交付结果。

useCases.title: Hermes Agent的使用场景
useCases.description: 每周简报需要新来源，成熟方法需要维护者，稍后续接的任务只需必要决定和证据。Hermes Agent 可用于研究这些连续性机制，使长期知识与临时会话背景各有保留边界。

items.title: 重复性研究简报
items.description: 周期性研究简报需要获得新资料，同时保留原有研究范围。定义每周新增来源如何进入流程、如何标注时效，以及引用怎样保留在摘要中。复用规则维持稳定的交付要求，也要容纳不同周期真正发生变化的研究发现。

items.title: 可复用工作方法
items.description: 成熟工作方法转为任务知识时，需要明确假设和维护责任。使用反例审查流程，整理成记忆或 Skill 草稿，并说明条件变化后由谁更新。保存下来的知识应持续可审阅，避免过时指令在后续任务中长期累积和重复使用。

items.title: 稍后继续的任务
items.description: 稍后继续任务时，最重要的是决定下一步行动的既有决定和证据。围绕暂停状态提取这些必要信息，排除无关对话历史。续接记录应让下一个会话理解哪些事项已经确定、哪些仍待处理，以及支持判断的资料在哪里。

items.title: 来源变化后复核已有知识
items.description: 可复用方法可能依赖已经过时的来源、条件或决定。将保留的任务知识与新材料对照，标明需要重新审阅的假设。参考 Hermes Agent 的连续性思路时，也要约定由谁接受更新，以及如何区分旧指引和后续任务真正应该采用的版本。

faq.question: Hermes Agent 与 Skill 集合有什么区别？
faq.answer: Hermes 是运行中的 Agent 系统。Skills 只是它保存可复用任务知识的一种方式，系统还包含记忆、工具和调度等部分；单纯的指令集合不能代替这些运行能力。

faq.question: 持久记忆就是聊天记录吗？
faq.answer: 不是。项目将持久记忆与对话上下文分别说明。评估时应了解存储了什么、如何复用，以及怎样纠正或移除信息。

faq.question: 保存成 Skill 就代表方法可靠吗？
faq.answer: 不代表。可复用方法仍可能包含过时假设或特定任务中的错误，应检查来源、依赖和实际结果，再决定是否作为稳定流程使用。

faq.question: Hermes 能连接 MCP 工具吗？
faq.answer: 官方文档包含 MCP 集成。实际可用服务取决于服务器配置、凭证和访问规则，支持协议不等于自动获得所有服务权限。

faq.question: 借鉴这些机制是否需要更换工作工具？
faq.answer: 不需要。可以先将 Hermes Agent 作为任务结构、工具边界和结果审阅的设计参考，在已有工作流中验证思路。软件复用是另一项选择，需要核对兼容性、权限与许可；借鉴设计思路不会自动完成软件与 Floatboat 的连接。

faq.question: Hermes Agent 由谁维护，源码采用什么许可？
faq.answer: 官方仓库由 Nous Research 发布，源码采用 MIT 许可。接入的模型服务与外部系统有各自的访问条件和商业条款。

howTo.title: 维护 Hermes Agent 多次执行中的知识
howTo.description: 知识能被保存，并不代表它适合长期复用。区分稳定方法与临时会话背景，约定维护者和更新方式，再用重复任务中的新证据检查记忆及续接设计是否可靠。

items.title: 分类需要保留的信息
items.description: 引入记忆机制前，先区分临时背景、长期事实、决策与流程。

items.title: 约定纠正与交付方式
items.description: 为知识设置更新方式，为重复任务明确时间、输出位置和失败路径。

items.title: 评估多次运行结果
items.description: 检查输入变化后流程是否仍准确，而非只凭一次成功判断效果。

zh.seoDescription: 研究 Hermes Agent 的记忆、可复用 Skills、工具与调度，了解上下文延续和方法存储如何支持重复工作，再结合自己的任务与环境判断持续执行和人工审阅方式。

en.seoTitle: Kimi Code CLI: Subagents, Hooks, and Coding Workflow Handoffs
en.description: Study Kimi Code CLI’s tool loop, focused subagents, lifecycle hooks, and editor protocol as references for your own workflows. Use them to clarify task roles, execution checks, and context handoffs around work in Floatboat.
overview: Kimi Code CLI is Moonshot AI’s current open-source coding agent for the terminal. Its official description includes reading and editing code, running commands, searching files, and fetching web pages, with the agent choosing subsequent steps from tool feedback. It is an application around the model, not a Skill package.

For a Floatboat user improving a workflow, the useful ideas are role separation, explicit tool feedback, and well-defined points for checks. Kimi Code CLI provides a concrete reference for those mechanisms. ACP also illustrates how an interface can remain separate from the process that executes an agent task.

The maintained repository is MoonshotAI/kimi-code and uses MIT. The earlier Python project, MoonshotAI/kimi-cli, was archived and directs users to the newer CLI. Keep that distinction in mind when reading tutorials: the old project’s architecture, package names, and instructions are not interchangeable with the current release.
en.capabilitiesTitle: Workflow Mechanisms to Learn From
en.capabilitiesIntro: Kimi Code's tool-feedback loop, delegated responsibilities, and lifecycle checks solve different coordination problems. Review their interfaces as parts of an execution design, with the context and review evidence each role must return made explicit before tasks move between stages.

capabilities.title: An explicit tool-feedback loop
capabilities.description: Study how a task continues from command and file results, then define the evidence your own workflow needs at each step.

capabilities.title: Focused task responsibilities
capabilities.description: Use subagent contexts as a reference for dividing exploration, planning, and implementation without losing the parent task’s goal.

capabilities.title: Checks at lifecycle boundaries
capabilities.description: Study hooks and interface protocols when deciding where to validate an action and how context should pass between tools.

useCases.title: Use Cases for Kimi Code CLI
useCases.description: Role delegation, pre-action checks, and editor handoffs create different coordination requirements. Explore Kimi Code's interface and runtime boundaries while defining each role's output, review point, and context contract before testing compatibility with your existing environment.

items.title: A multi-role coding workflow
items.description: A coding workflow can divide research, planning, and implementation into distinct roles. Define each role's inputs, inspectable outputs, and handoff conditions within the same development task. Include the conditions for returning findings to the main task so parallel contributions do not become disconnected assignments.

items.title: Checks before consequential steps
items.description: Before a consequential command, file change, or external action, decide what evidence is needed to assess its impact. Place a validation or human review point there and return the result to the workflow. Whether execution continues or stops should follow the applicable authorization and the check's actual findings.

items.title: A consistent context handoff
items.description: A workflow spanning an editor, workspace, and agent process needs a clear context contract between them. Use the interface–runtime separation to map workspace paths and task information to the execution process. Verify the ACP or other interface handoff rather than assuming a client supports the required behavior natively.

items.title: Evaluate a lifecycle check before adoption
items.description: A hook or plugin intended to inspect a consequential step needs its own bounded trial. Compare the maintained Kimi Code documentation with the surrounding runtime and describe what the check receives, returns, and does when it cannot decide. Verify that its feedback reaches the main workflow without assuming that merely installing an extension creates the approval policy your project requires.

faq.question: Which Kimi repository is current?
faq.answer: Use MoonshotAI/kimi-code for Kimi Code CLI. MoonshotAI/kimi-cli is the archived Python implementation and explicitly directs users to the current project.

faq.question: Is Kimi Code CLI an independent agent project?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an interactive application, tools, sessions, and agent execution. It is not just a prompt, a model, or a collection of Skills, even though Skills can extend its workflows.

faq.question: Can it use a provider other than Kimi?
faq.answer: The README says other compatible providers can be configured. Verify the provider’s protocol and feature support rather than assuming that every model endpoint behaves identically.

faq.question: What does ACP integration provide?
faq.answer: It allows compatible editors to drive a Kimi Code CLI session over the Agent Client Protocol. The editor supplies its interface while the CLI handles the agent session; the editor must support the integration.

faq.question: Must I switch products to use these workflow ideas?
faq.answer: No. You can first use Kimi Code CLI as a reference for task structure, tool boundaries, and result review in your existing workflow. Reusing software is a separate choice that requires compatibility, permissions, and license checks; applying the design ideas does not automatically connect the software to Floatboat.

faq.question: Does MIT cover a Kimi subscription?
faq.answer: No. MIT applies to the project source. Kimi Code account access, Moonshot API use, and any other provider’s service are governed by their own entitlements, limits, and terms.

prerequisites.title: Use the current Kimi Code reference
prerequisites.description: The maintained kimi-code reference and legacy Python CLI examples may describe different architectures. Establish which version the investigation concerns before reusing delegation or context mechanisms, and read the matching documentation rather than combining incompatible examples into one setup.

items.title: Use the maintained reference
items.description: Use kimi-code documentation when studying the mechanisms; legacy Python CLI examples can describe a different architecture.

howTo.title: Verify delegated work in Kimi Code
howTo.description: Delegated coding work should preserve enough context for the next role without passing unrelated history. Define the handoff contract and review point for each contribution, then verify that the receiving stage can use the actual material before extending the workflow.

items.title: Define each role and checkpoint
items.description: Specify what each delegated task receives, what it returns, and which operation must wait for review.

items.title: Test the context transfer
items.description: Check whether each stage gets enough relevant information without carrying unrelated conversation history into every step.

en.seoDescription: Study Kimi Code CLI’s subagents, hooks, and tool-feedback loop. Design clearer roles, context handoffs, and execution checks while separating runtime setup from model access.

zh.seoTitle: Kimi Code CLI：子 Agent、Hooks 与编程任务交接
zh.description: 参考 Kimi Code CLI 的工具循环、子 Agent、生命周期 hooks 与编辑器协议，为自己的工作流划分任务职责、设置执行检查，并改善 Floatboat 中各环节的上下文交接。
overview: Kimi Code CLI 是月之暗面当前的开源终端编程 Agent。官方说明涵盖读取和编辑代码、执行命令、搜索文件与获取网页，再根据工具反馈选择后续步骤。它是模型周围的应用系统，不是一个 Skill 包。
对希望优化工作流的 Floatboat 用户，有价值的是职责划分、明确的工具反馈和适当的检查节点。Kimi Code CLI 为这些机制提供了具体参考；ACP 也展示了界面与 Agent 执行进程分离的组织方式。
当前维护的仓库是 MoonshotAI/kimi-code，采用 MIT 许可。旧 Python 项目 MoonshotAI/kimi-cli 已归档并引导迁移到新版。阅读教程时要区分版本，旧架构、包名和命令不能直接当作当前发行版说明。
zh.capabilitiesTitle: 值得借鉴的工作流机制
zh.capabilitiesIntro: Kimi Code 通过工具反馈、角色职责和生命周期检查协调执行。每个角色交回的上下文及审阅证据需要足以支撑下一阶段，接口存在并不能代替这些交接约定。

capabilities.title: 明确工具反馈循环
capabilities.description: 研究任务如何依据命令和文件结果继续，明确自己的流程各步骤需要什么证据。

capabilities.title: 专注的任务职责
capabilities.description: 参考子 Agent 上下文划分探索、规划与实施职责，同时保留主任务目标。

capabilities.title: 生命周期边界上的检查
capabilities.description: 需要确定操作检查节点和工具间上下文传递方式时，研究 hooks 与接口协议。

useCases.title: Kimi Code CLI的使用场景
useCases.description: 多角色编码要约定成果交接，重要动作要设置检查点，编辑器还需传递正确背景。Kimi Code 的接口与运行时机制可作为参考，具体上下文约定及适配仍应在自己的环境验证。

items.title: 多角色开发流程
items.description: 编码工作流可以将研究、规划和实施交给不同角色，但需要定义各自输入、可检查的输出和交接条件。所有角色围绕同一个开发任务协作，并约定何时将发现返回主任务，避免并行贡献逐渐变成彼此脱节的独立工作。

items.title: 重要步骤之前的检查
items.description: 在有实际影响的命令、文件变更或外部行动之前，明确评估影响需要哪些证据，并设置验证或人工审阅节点。将检查结果带回工作流，再依据实际发现和适用授权决定继续或停止，而不是仅根据原有计划自动执行。

items.title: 一致的上下文交接
items.description: 跨编辑器、工作区和 Agent 进程的任务，需要清楚的上下文传递约定。参考界面与运行时分离的方式，将工作区路径和任务资料对应到执行进程。对 ACP 或其他接口进行实际核验，不假定客户端天然支持所需的全部行为。

items.title: 采用生命周期检查前先试验
items.description: 用于检查重要步骤的钩子或插件，本身也需要范围明确的试验。对照当前 Kimi Code 文档及外围运行环境，说明检查接收什么、返回什么，以及无法判断时如何处理。验证反馈能够回到主流程，不假定安装扩展就已经建立项目需要的批准策略。

faq.question: 现在应选择哪个 Kimi 仓库？
faq.answer: 当前应使用 MoonshotAI/kimi-code。MoonshotAI/kimi-cli 是已归档的 Python 实现，其官方说明明确引导用户迁移到新项目。

faq.question: Kimi Code CLI 属于独立 Agent 项目吗？
faq.answer: 是。它包含交互应用、工具、会话和 Agent 执行能力，不能只理解为提示、模型或 Skill 集合；Skills 可以参与其中，但不是整个项目。

faq.question: 是否只能使用 Kimi 模型？
faq.answer: README 说明可配置其他兼容提供方。实际使用前仍要核对协议与功能支持，不能假设所有模型接口行为一致。

faq.question: ACP 集成提供什么？
faq.answer: 它让兼容编辑器通过 Agent Client Protocol 驱动 Kimi Code CLI 会话。编辑器提供界面，CLI 承担 Agent 会话，前提是编辑器支持相关集成。

faq.question: 借鉴这些机制是否需要更换工作工具？
faq.answer: 不需要。可以先将 Kimi Code CLI 作为任务结构、工具边界和结果审阅的设计参考，在已有工作流中验证思路。软件复用是另一项选择，需要核对兼容性、权限与许可；借鉴设计思路不会自动完成软件与 Floatboat 的连接。

faq.question: MIT 许可是否覆盖 Kimi 订阅？
faq.answer: 不覆盖。MIT 适用于项目源码；Kimi Code 账号访问、Moonshot API 调用和其他模型服务分别适用各自权益、额度与条款。

prerequisites.title: 使用当前 Kimi Code 资料
prerequisites.description: 持续维护的 kimi-code 与旧 Python CLI 示例可能描述不同架构。以下条件先确定调查针对哪个版本，再借鉴委派或上下文机制，避免把不兼容示例混合成一套配置。

items.title: 选择当前维护的参考
items.description: 研究机制时使用 kimi-code 文档，旧 Python CLI 示例可能属于不同架构。

howTo.title: 验证 Kimi Code 中的委派任务
howTo.description: 下一角色既需要足够背景，也不应被无关历史淹没。为委派贡献约定输出和审阅节点，再检查接收阶段能否使用实际材料，确认交接有效后才扩展更多协作环节。

items.title: 定义职责与检查点
items.description: 明确每个委派任务接收什么、返回什么，以及哪些操作必须等待审阅。

items.title: 验证上下文传递
items.description: 检查各阶段是否获得足够相关信息，同时避免每一步都携带无关对话历史。

zh.seoDescription: 研究 Kimi Code CLI 的子 Agent、hooks 与工具反馈循环，为自己的编程工作设计职责、上下文交接和执行检查，并分别核对运行配置、模型接入及相关使用条件。

en.seoTitle: ZCode: Coding Workbench, Harness Layers, and Human Review
en.description: Study ZCode’s workbench and agent-runtime design to improve your own workflows. Use its interface separation and public source as references for organizing task context, execution feedback, and human review around work in Floatboat.
overview: ZCode is Z.ai’s coding-agent harness and development workbench. The official repository describes desktop, browser, and terminal experiences, and includes client code, backend services, shared UI, and the agent CLI and runtime. It is broader than an editor plugin or a single task instruction.

Its value as a workflow reference is the relationship between the interface, backend services, and agent execution. A Floatboat user can study those boundaries to decide where context should enter, how a task’s progress should be presented, and when the user should review a proposed action. Actual reuse requires a separately verified integration.

The public source uses Apache-2.0 and the repository also provides a project notice covering additional operational and third-party matters. Source availability does not settle model access, hosted service terms, or every application behavior. Review the official notice and release documentation for the version you choose.
en.capabilitiesTitle: Workflow Mechanisms to Learn From
en.capabilitiesIntro: ZCode separates interface presentation from execution while making task progress available for review. Compare the project material, current activity, and surrounding system responsibilities before borrowing its structure, so a visible status does not replace evidence about the resulting work.

capabilities.title: Separate interface and execution
capabilities.description: Study the workbench’s layers when deciding which part of a workflow should collect context and which part should execute the task.

capabilities.title: Make task progress reviewable
capabilities.description: Use the application structure as a reference for presenting agent activity alongside the context a person needs to judge it.

capabilities.title: Inspect the complete system
capabilities.description: Read client, backend, CLI, and runtime source together when evaluating a workflow pattern rather than copying an isolated interface.

useCases.title: Use Cases for ZCode
useCases.description: Long-running projects, human approval, and multiple interfaces need a clear owner for task state. Use ZCode to examine how materials, current activity, and proposed results remain connected without confusing a visible execution log with an understandable review artifact.

items.title: A task-centered workspace
items.description: Long-running work needs source material, working directories, and expected deliverables to stay connected. Describe how the current activity relates to those inputs and how task state is retained as work progresses. The workspace design should make it possible to trace a result back through the activity that produced it.

items.title: A human review point
items.description: A person reviewing an agent's proposed edit or external operation needs more than an execution log. Identify the relevant context, the change being proposed, and the evidence that supports accepting it. Build those artifacts into the review point so approval rests on an understandable result.

items.title: A workflow across interfaces
items.description: When a task appears through desktop, web, and terminal interfaces, decide which layer owns state and which performs execution. Map the shared task information and the responsibilities of each entry point, then check consistency between them. Multiple views should not silently become competing versions of the same work.

items.title: Map where task information is processed
items.description: A desktop interface can present work whose data or execution crosses another service boundary. Use ZCode's project notice and source as references to identify what is local, what is remote, and which component receives each piece of context. Apply that map to your own workspace design before providing sensitive material or deciding how approvals should accompany the execution path.

faq.question: Does ZCode include a real agent harness?
faq.answer: Yes. The official project identifies ZCode as a coding-agent harness, and the repository includes the agent CLI and runtime alongside its application code. It is not merely a third-party skin around a model API.

faq.question: Is ZCode only a desktop application?
faq.answer: No. The repository documents desktop, browser, and terminal interfaces. Check the selected interface’s requirements rather than assuming a configuration for one entry point works unchanged in another.

faq.question: Who publishes the official ZCode repository?
faq.answer: The official repository is zai-org/ZCode under Z.ai. Community forks, including similarly named workbenches, should be identified by their own maintainers and changes rather than treated as the same official release.

faq.question: What does the source license cover?
faq.answer: The repository is Apache-2.0 licensed. Third-party notices, model APIs, hosted services, and distribution-specific conditions still need separate review; the repository includes NOTICE.md for relevant project declarations.

faq.question: Can model quality alone explain ZCode results?
faq.answer: No. Tool configuration, context assembly, the execution environment, and how changes are reviewed also affect the outcome. Compare the complete workflow for the task rather than treating the model name as the result.

faq.question: Must I switch products to use these workflow ideas?
faq.answer: No. You can first use ZCode as a reference for task structure, tool boundaries, and result review in your existing workflow. Reusing software is a separate choice that requires compatibility, permissions, and license checks; applying the design ideas does not automatically connect the software to Floatboat.

prerequisites.title: Check ZCode’s data boundaries
prerequisites.description: Local and remote execution can expose task information to different recipients. Use ZCode's source and project notice to identify those boundaries before supplying material, with the actual service path checked separately from what the desktop interface appears to contain.

items.title: Check data and execution boundaries
items.description: Use the project notice and source to assess what is local, what is remote, and which service receives task information.

howTo.title: Prototype a ZCode review loop
howTo.description: A workflow spanning task context, interaction, and tools needs those responsibilities assigned before expansion. Test one complete, reviewable result first, then use its evidence to decide where another interface or tool would add value without splitting the task state.

items.title: Map the layers of the task
items.description: Separate business context, user interaction, execution tools, and the result that must be reviewed.

items.title: Prototype the review loop
items.description: Test one task from input to a reviewable result before expanding the workflow across more tools or interfaces.

en.seoDescription: Explore ZCode’s coding workbench and runtime layers. Connect task context, tool execution, and human review while keeping interface, harness, and model-provider roles clear.

zh.seoTitle: ZCode：编程工作台、Harness 分层与人工审阅
zh.description: 参考 ZCode 的工作台与 Agent 运行时设计，优化自己工作流中的任务背景、执行反馈和人工审阅。结合公开源码与不同交互入口，评估适合 Floatboat 工作方式的组织机制。
overview: ZCode 是 Z.ai 的编程 Agent Harness 与开发工作台。官方仓库介绍桌面、浏览器和终端体验，包含客户端、后端服务、共享 UI、Agent CLI 与运行时源码，范围大于单个编辑器插件或任务指令。
它作为工作流参考的价值，在于界面、后端服务与 Agent 执行之间的关系。Floatboat 用户可以据此思考上下文从哪里进入、任务过程如何呈现，以及何时需要人工审阅操作；实际复用仍需单独验证集成方式。
公开源码采用 Apache-2.0，仓库另有项目声明说明运行和第三方事项。源码公开不能代替模型访问、托管服务条款或应用行为的具体判断，应结合所选版本阅读官方声明和发行说明。
zh.capabilitiesTitle: 值得借鉴的工作流机制
zh.capabilitiesIntro: 可见进度需要与项目资料和实际执行对应，才足以支持审阅。ZCode 对界面和运行职责的划分提供系统参考；状态正在变化，并不等于交付结果已经达到要求。

capabilities.title: 区分界面与执行
capabilities.description: 研究工作台的层次，明确流程中哪些部分负责收集背景，哪些负责执行任务。

capabilities.title: 让任务过程可审阅
capabilities.description: 参考应用组织方式，将 Agent 活动与用户作出判断所需的上下文一起呈现。

capabilities.title: 研究完整系统关系
capabilities.description: 评估流程模式时结合客户端、后端、CLI 与运行层理解，避免只复制孤立界面。

useCases.title: ZCode的使用场景
useCases.description: 长任务需要让资料、当前活动和结果始终关联，人工批准又依赖清楚的审阅材料。ZCode 可供研究这些连接及多界面职责，使用户知道正在接受什么，而不只看到执行日志。

items.title: 以任务为中心的工作区
items.description: 较长任务中，原始资料、工作目录和目标交付物需要始终保持关联。说明当前活动如何使用这些输入，以及推进过程中怎样保留任务状态。工作空间设计应能够从最终结果追溯到产生它的操作，而不是只展示当前正在发生的动作。

items.title: 人工审阅节点
items.description: 审阅 Agent 提出的修改或外部操作时，使用者需要的不只是执行日志。应明确相关上下文、拟议变更及支持接受它的证据，并将这些材料组织到审阅节点中。批准行为建立在能够理解的结果上，而不是一串难以判断含义的运行记录。

items.title: 跨入口的工作流
